A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MoScale research work. All 12 pages, including equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–B, are readable and support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark results, user studies, and ablations in Section 5, plus tokenizer reconstruction results in Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark results, user studies, ablations, and appendix reconstruction results.

M1.justification: The next-scale autoregressive model, hierarchical and temporal refinement, training losses, inference procedure, and residual VQ-VAE architecture are unchanged in Section 4 and Appendix B.

E1.justification: Both versions use HumanML3D and KIT-ML and retain the same text-to-motion and zero-shot scenarios. The revised HumanML3D sequence count does not establish different dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within Tables 1–3 and the qualitative and user-study comparisons. The zero-shot comparisons still use BAMM and MoMask.

E3.justification: Section 5 changes the reported HumanML3D size from 14,515 to 14,616 motion sequences. The 44,970 text descriptions, split proportions, preprocessing, metrics, and training settings remain unchanged. This is a revision to the reported sample count; the PDFs do not establish that experiments were rerun or additional sequences were actually used.

E4.justification: The text-complexity analysis, refinement and generation-order ablations, corruption-rate and depth studies, iteration and guidance analyses, and Appendix A visualizations are unchanged.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains averages over 20 runs with 95% confidence intervals. Uncertainty reporting elsewhere in the main text and appendix is also unchanged.

E6.justification: All benchmark scores, user-study outcomes, ablation results, plots, and appendix reconstruction results are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains MoScale S=18 Top-1 accuracy of 0.540 and FID of 0.046. The dataset-size edit is descriptive metadata, not a changed experimental outcome.

T1.justification: The autoregressive factorizations, mathematical definitions, and residual quantization and refinement equations in Sections 3–4 are identical. No theoretical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about hierarchical generation, improved semantic alignment, training efficiency, scaling, and zero-shot capabilities.

C2.justification: Interpretations of hierarchical refinement, temporal coherence, efficiency tradeoffs, and coarse-to-fine representations remain unchanged. Neither version adds or revises applicability boundaries or limitations.

D1.justification: Implementation instructions, hyperparameters, training-time information, preprocessing procedures, and Appendix B architecture details are unchanged. The project/code-access link also remains identical.

R1.justification: The 61 references and the related-work discussion are unchanged, including positioning relative to next-token autoregression, diffusion, masked transformers, and prior next-scale modeling.

P1.justification: The arXiv margin stamp changes from v1 dated 4 April 2026 to v2 dated 26 May 2026. Apart from the dataset-count edit, the prose, terminology, headings, and document structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–6, Tables 1–5, captions, axes, legends, and page composition are unchanged. Rendered-page differences are confined to the version/date text and the dataset-count digits.

improvement.justification: The only scientific-text revision is the HumanML3D count changing from 14,515 to 14,616 in Section 5; the PDFs do not independently establish which count is correct. With methods, evidence, explanations, reproducibility instructions, and appendices otherwise unchanged, this isolated edit and the version/date update produce no meaningful overall quality difference.
